Pricing and billing

1% of verified savings, monthly. Nothing else. No subscription, no seats, no minimum, no setup fee. Installing and running MESH is free and needs no account. A fee exists only after we have agreed billing with you in writing, and only for months in which MESH actually saved you money.

What it costs

The fee is 1% of the net verified savings in a calendar month. You keep the other 99%.

These rows are arithmetic to show the scale, not results:

Your monthly LLM spendIf MESH saves 10%If MESH saves 20%If MESH saves 40%
$10,000fee $10fee $20fee $40
$100,000fee $100fee $200fee $400
$1,000,000fee $1,000fee $2,000fee $4,000

What you would save depends on the shape of your traffic. The measured ranges, each with its label and the command that reproduces it, are on Savings by segment and Evidence. Some setups save nothing, and then the fee is nothing.

When nothing is due

  • You have not agreed billing with us. Use MESH as long as you like.
  • The month's verdict is do_not_charge. That is the outcome when net savings are zero or negative, or when 1% of them comes to less than one cent.
  • The saving was already yours. Savings from caching you had switched on yourself, at your provider or your gateway, are itemised and left out.
  • The work failed. Savings on a task that did not complete are not counted.
  • We could not price it. A request on a model or date that is not in the published price list is excluded. It is never counted as a saving.

A lever that cost you money in a month is set against the ones that saved you money in that month. Our losses reduce the fee; they are not hidden.

The fee is rounded down to the cent, so it is never more than 1%.

How to start paying

  • Try it first. Run MESH on your own traffic and look at the result: mesh status for the running total, mesh verify to re-check the ledger.
  • Tell us. If the saving is worth having, open an issue with the title "Billing". Please do not post your figures or your ledger in a public issue; we reply with a private way to continue.
  • Agree it in writing. We settle who the customer is, the billing month, the currency, and where invoices go. Until that exists, no fee is due.

What happens each month

After the month ends, you run one command on the machine where MESH runs:

mesh statement --period 2026-11

It re-checks your ledger's hash chain, recomputes the month, prints the savings by lever and the fee, and writes a statement file. Then:

  • You send us the statement file and the ledger files it was made from. They hold usage numbers, lever names, model names and hashes. They never hold your prompts, your answers or your API key. Open them and look before you send them.
  • We recompute the same figure from the same ledger and send you a statement and an invoice. We do not take payment automatically.
  • If your number and ours differ for the same ledger, yours wins.

The billing month is the calendar month in UTC: a request counts in the month it started in. mesh verify and mesh status show the total since you installed MESH, not one month; the month's figure is the one on the statement.

What "verified" means

Each saving is the difference between two costs for the same request.

  • What you paid comes from the usage your provider reported back for that request, priced at the provider's published rate for that day.
  • What you would have paid is worked out by MESH: the tokens it removed from the request before sending it, priced at the same rate. On the statement these rows are labelled *estimated baseline*, because the request that was not sent has no provider reading.
  • Where a saving can be read directly from the provider's own figures, such as a cheaper processing tier, its row is labelled *measured*.

The rules are published in full in the methodology. The ledger, the price list and the arithmetic are all on your machine, so you can check every line without trusting us.

Currency and tax

Figures are computed in US dollars, the currency the providers price in. The invoice currency is set in the billing agreement. Fees exclude VAT and similar taxes, which are added where they apply.

If you disagree with an invoice

Recompute it. mesh statement --check <file> tells you whether a statement file has been altered since it was written, and mesh statement --period rebuilds the month from your ledger. If the figures do not match ours, send us yours and we use it. The contract terms are in the Terms.
